outcome: Filed November 23, 2021; docket terminated November 12, 2024. Apple reported as having voluntarily dismissed the suit in September 2024, citing risk that continued litigation would expose its threat-intelligence program.

A Greek court convicted Tal Dilian (Intellexa founder), Sara Hamou, Felix Bitzios and Yiannis Lavranos of breaching the confidentiality of telephone communications and illegally accessing information systems in connection with 2020-2021 Predator surveillance of 90+ Greek public figures; each was sentenced to eight years in prison (aggregate per-defendant sentences reported as 126 years 8 months, actual time capped at eight years), suspended pending appeal. Dilian said the conviction was unfounded, that he would not be a 'scapegoat', and that he would appeal; an appeal hearing was set for December 2026. Separately, in July 2026 eight wiretapping victims sued Intellexa SA seeking 1M euros each in moral damages.
title: Greek court convicts Intellexa founder Tal Dilian and three others over Predatorgate wiretapping (Athens)
